rationale: Start with a broad mid-strength scouting gradient at moderate temperature to capture all 10 compounds without likely truncation while revealing the overall retention window and any severe critical pairs. This gives a balanced first map of retention and selectivity before refining slope, range, and temperature.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing analysis time. Shortening the same broad gradient should pull the last peak earlier while likely preserving adequate resolution, giving a direct read on how much speed margin we have.

We are very close to the 10 min target and still have resolution margin at the critical 6/7 pair, so the next efficient move is another one-step gradient shortening. This tests whether we can eliminate the remaining time penalty without sacrificing full resolution.

At 14 min the only issue is a slight shortfall in the critical pair, so keep the fast gradient and adjust selectivity with a modest temperature decrease. Lowering T often restores some resolution while likely keeping the last peak within 10 min or very close to it.

Temperature worsened selectivity, so return to 40 C and instead make the gradient slightly shallower by lowering phi1 one step. This should preferentially spread the later cluster around peaks 5–10, potentially lifting the 6/7 pair above 1.5 while keeping t_last near 10 min.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now the goal is to see whether an even faster method can preserve full resolution and stay at or under 10 min. Shortening tG by one step from the optimal resolved condition is the cleanest boundary test; if a pair drops below 1.5, injection 5 remains the best.

Since shortening tG broke the critical 6/7 pair, keep tG at 14 min and slightly lower phi1 again to make the late part of the gradient shallower. This may preserve full resolution while nudging selectivity and retention just enough to identify whether injection 5 is the true optimum or if there is a neighboring plateau.

The optimum appears localized near injection 5, so now test whether narrowing the gradient window from the front can trim early dead space without hurting the critical late pair. Raising phi0 one step while keeping phi1 and tG fixed probes whether all peaks can be compressed slightly yet still remain fully resolved and within 10 min.

Injection 8 improved speed while keeping full resolution, so continue pushing the front of the gradient one step stronger to see if more early compression is possible. This tests whether we can retain CRF 1.000 with an even shorter effective separation window before the 6/7 pair or early peaks begin to suffer.

Phi0 0.15 with phi1 0.85 and tG 14 is a confirmed optimum-class method, so the next useful probe is a small temperature increase to see whether we can retain full resolution while gaining additional speed. This selectively tests whether 45 C improves or preserves the critical 6/7 separation better than the stronger phi0 change did.

Higher temperature clearly hurts the critical pair, so stay at 40 C and instead test a slightly steeper late gradient from the best phi0 = 0.15 condition. This checks whether phi1 = 0.90 gives a similar or better selectivity balance than phi1 = 0.85 while remaining within the no-penalty time window.

The best region is clearly centered at phi0 0.15 and 40 C, with the 6/7 pair setting the limit. Testing phi1 one step lower from the best method checks whether a slightly shallower late gradient can add a bit more resolution margin while still staying under 10 min.

We already have CRF 1.000, so remaining experiments should map robustness around the optimum rather than chase impossible improvement. Lengthening tG one step from the best method will show how much resolution reserve exists at the critical pair and confirm whether injection 8 sits at the practical speed limit.

Around the optimum, phi0 has shown the strongest control over the critical 6/7 pair, so the remaining informative direction is to lower phi0 one step from injection 5 while keeping the rest fixed. This will test whether a slightly weaker start can add extra resolution margin without pushing the last peak beyond 10 min.

We have already mapped phi0, phi1, tG, and higher temperature near the optimum; the one remaining broad orthogonal check is the low-temperature extreme. This will show whether the strong temperature sensitivity of the 6/7 pair can ever be exploited beneficially, while avoiding repetition of methods already tested.

The low-temperature run showed strong, different selectivity changes, so a moderate cooling from the best phi0 0.15 / phi1 0.85 condition is the most informative remaining compromise. Pair 6/7 is the limiting pair at 40 C, and 35 C may improve it enough to allow the faster 12 min gradient without losing full resolution.

A modest temperature reduction changed the limiting pair from 6/7 to 5/6, indicating strong non-monotonic selectivity effects; probing 30 C will map that transition and test whether a different balance can rescue the faster 12 min gradient. This is a high-information adjacent condition around the best region without repeating any prior method.

The map now strongly indicates 40 C is the only useful temperature and the optimum lies near phi0 0.10–0.15, phi1 0.85, tG 14; the remaining key boundary is whether an even shorter gradient is decisively too fast. Testing tG 10 at the best phi0/phi1/T condition will define the speed limit around the optimum and confirm robustness of injection 8 as the practical choice.

With tG fixed at the successful 14 min and 40 C clearly optimal, the last untested adjacent gradient-window refinement is a lower phi1 from the best phi0 = 0.15 condition. This checks whether a slightly shallower late gradient can preserve full resolution while keeping t_last at or below 10 min, potentially revealing another 1.000 method.

The only remaining local comparison around the two optimal 1.000 methods is whether the phi0 = 0.10 version responds differently to a small temperature increase than the phi0 = 0.15 version did. This probes interaction between phi0 and temperature near the optimum while still staying close to the best-performing region.

The best methods are already identified, so use remaining injections to bracket the response surface near them. Increasing phi1 one step beyond previously tested values from the phi0 = 0.10 optimum checks whether stronger late elution can preserve enough resolution while further reducing retention, clarifying the upper phi1 boundary.

This is the corresponding upper-phi1 boundary test from the other confirmed optimum at phi0 = 0.15. It completes the local map around the best methods and checks whether the slightly stronger start tolerates a stronger late gradient differently with respect to the limiting 6/7 pair.

The optimum region is already established, so use a remaining shot to complete the temperature trend above 45 C at the best phi0/phi1/tG condition. This confirms whether resolution collapse of the critical 6/7 pair continues monotonically with temperature and closes out the local robustness map.

With only two injections left and the optimum already secured, use one to extend the temperature trend at a nearby condition where extra gradient time may partially offset the loss of selectivity. This helps distinguish whether higher temperature mainly changes selectivity or whether added shallowing can rescue it in the phi0 = 0.10 family.

For the final run, complete the matched comparison to injection 24 in the other 1.000-method family. This last adjacent test cleanly separates phi0 and temperature effects near the optimum, while the campaign already secures the best methods at injections 5 and 8.
